transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Time: 10:00 PDT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Lopez (VantageMed CTO), Devon Kim (Platform Eng), Priya Ramesh (Security), Alex Morgan (SRE)

---
Summary: Weekly POC check-in for Redwood Private (VPC) pilot. Focus on networking connectivity to control plane, KV cache warmup behavior, next upgrade to runtime and planned benchmarks.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, and then we'll dig into the network checklist items.
[00:12] Sara Lopez: hi all, Sara here. we did a quick internal smoke earlier this morning, still seeing the same fail for the control plane connection. it times out when the agent tries to fetch model manifest.
[00:23] Leo Patel: ok that's helpful — can you confirm whether the attempt is going through the fwd proxy or direct from the VPC? sometimes proxy rewrite causes cert handshake issues.
[00:36] Alex Morgan: yeah it's going through the corp forward-proxy. Devon and I pinned the tcp dumps. it looks like the TLS SNI is being rewritten, so the control plane sees a mismatch, then the agent falls back and retries which times out.
[00:50] Devon Kim: there's also a misconfig on the egress ACLs, we hadn't allowed outbound to redwood-control.redwoodai.com on port 443 from the worker subnets.
[01:05] Maya Chen: that maps to the checklist item we sent last week, sorry if that doc wasn't clear — i'll resend an updated network checklist after this call with explicit CIDR ranges and example iptables rules.
[01:17] Priya Ramesh: important for us is that outbound goes to STS/KMS endpoints as well — our KMS is in a different account and there are cross-account policies. we can't open wide 0.0.0.0/0 egress.
[01:31] Leo Patel: understood. the private deployment supports customer-managed KMS, and the agent will call the KMS endpoints directly — we can provide the exact hostnames. i'll add those to the checklist.
[01:45] Sara Lopez: perfect. next, performance — we're seeing p99 latencies spike on cold KV cache after scale events.
[01:55] Leo Patel: yeah that sounds like KV cache warmup. for reference, our runtime keeps a per-shard KV cache and on scale-out the new nodes start cold, they do progressive prefetch but depending on prefix hit rates you can see p99 spikes for a few minutes.
[02:12] Devon Kim: we tried increasing the pre-warm threads but it didn't help much; there may also be tenant-level token burstiness.
[02:22] Maya Chen: can you share a trace from a spike window? the SE team (Leo) recommended running a workload replay with the same token distribution — we'll run that and compare.
[02:34] Alex Morgan: i uploaded some traces to the shared perf sheet, link in the doc. note that some timestamps in the agent logs show weird hostnames — maybe the host resolution was reading from an internal DNS view.
[02:47] Leo Patel: hmm DNS split-horizon can definitely affect hostnames for the control plane, that ties back to the TLS SNI problem. two birds. we'll include DNS resolution steps in the checklist too.
[02:58] Priya Ramesh: on the security side, we still need the SOC2 attachments and the audit log retention details — Redwood mentioned they could provide a retention config and sample logs.
[03:10] Maya Chen: yes, we'll send the SOC2 summary and a sample audit log schema. note that in Private mode audit logs can be shipped to your own S3/MinIO endpoint.
[03:22] Sara Lopez: good. also, question on upgrades — you mentioned 1.3.0 has some KV and routing fixes, what's the risk for our pilot?
[03:33] Leo Patel: v1.3.0 contains two key fixes: improved KV prefetch parallelism and a routing fallback path when SNI validation fails (reduces timeouts). upgrades are rolling and we can schedule a canary on a subset of nodes. risk is low but we advise a short maintenance window for egress rule checks.
[03:50] Devon Kim: what's the expected downtime during the rolling upgrade? we can't afford more than a few minutes of degraded throughput.
[03:58] Leo Patel: Rolling upgrades are usually zero-downtime for existing sessions — new nodes will join and old nodes drain. you might see transient p99 increases during cache repopulation, typically under 5 minutes for most workloads but depends on model seq length and token distribution.
[04:14] Maya Chen: we'll propose a maintenance window in the week of 2026-04-20; Leo will run the replay benchmark first and provide numbers so you can choose a low-traffic slot.
[04:26] Alex Morgan: sounds fine. Priya, any compliance blockers?
[04:30] Priya Ramesh: just two: encryption at rest verification for the standby disk images and log retention SLA. also we need the contact for a security engineer in case we need a deeper review.
[04:41] Maya Chen: i'll include the security engineer contact in the checklist email and attach the encryption doc.
[04:48] Sara Lopez: on cost — we ran a rough cost model and want to understand batching knobs and quantization options. can those be toggled per-deployment in the private control plane?
[05:00] Leo Patel: yes, batching and quantization profiles are configurable by route/model. for the pilot we usually start with conservative batch sizes and then tune. quantization depends on model; we can recommend a 4-bit profile for the smaller transformer variants which reduces token cost significantly.
[05:16] Devon Kim: any impact on accuracy if we switch to 4-bit for our summarization model?
[05:21] Leo Patel: minor, usually within margin, but we'll run an eval set as part of the replay. we'll compare ROUGE and a small human check set.
[05:31] Sara Lopez: ok good. recap of immediate blockers: egress rules & SNI rewrite, KMS endpoints, DNS resolution, and evidence for encryption/log retention.
[05:43] Maya Chen: agreed. action items: i'll send network checklist; Leo will run replay; Devon to confirm KMS egress; Priya to give retention numbers. we've captured those.
[05:56] Alex Morgan: one more small ask — can Redwood provide a short script to validate outbound connectivity from the worker host, like curl + cert check? that will speed ops validation.
[06:06] Leo Patel: yes we have a connectivity validator script. i'll attach it to the checklist and include example outputs.
[06:15] Sara Lopez: perfect. any questions from Redwood side?
[06:18] Maya Chen: none. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the checklist and proposed benchmark times.
[06:24] Devon Kim: thanks, bye.
[06:26] Priya Ramesh: thanks all.
[06:28] [call ends]

---
Notes: transcript contains a few small transcription artifacts (hostnames and product names sometimes mis-heard: "Redwood Privet" instead of Redwood Private). Frequent references to shared perf spreadsheet and network checklist.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
1) Redwood to resend network checklist with CIDRs, KMS hostnames and example iptables by 2026-04-10.
2) SE (Leo) to run workload replay and share results + latency/cost spreadsheet by 2026-04-12.
3) VantageMed infra (Devon) to confirm outbound rules for STS/KMS by 2026-04-14.
4) Schedule rolling runtime upgrade in week of 2026-04-20 after benchmarks.

End of file.
